findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query
findings.body: The deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls onSuccess, unlike disconnectMutation below it which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations on settle. When onChanged/onSuccess is undefined (or does not refetch), the parent keeps the old query data, so cacheUpdatedAt remains set, the 'Cache Status / Delete cached data' entry stays visible, and the user sees stale status immediately after a successful deletion.

findings.title: Cache status ignores cache expiry
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only serves rows with expiresAt >= now. Credentials whose cache expired (one month after write) will therefore still report a cacheUpdatedAt in connectedCalendars, display 'Cache Status' in the UI, and offer to delete data that is never actually served.

findings.title: Handler bypasses the calendar-cache disabled/mock repository path
findings.body: The handler directly instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository instead of going through the CalendarCache initialization that substitutes CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when calendar cache is disabled. Every connectedCalendars request now performs a CalendarCache groupBy query and can surface cache status even for users/organizations where the calendar-cache feature is disabled, adding an unconditional DB query to a hot settings endpoint.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US locale
findings.body: The timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) regardless of the user's configured locale obtained via useLocale. Non-English users will see US-style dates (e.g. MM/DD/YYYY) inconsistent with the rest of the localized UI.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts the wrong Prisma input type
findings.body: The method types data as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput but passes it to prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany, which expects SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput. UpdateInput permits nested relation operations (e.g. user: { connect }) that updateMany cannot execute, so the public repository signature promises operations that will fail or fail type-checking at the Prisma call; it should use the UpdateMany mutation input type.

findings.title: sed in-place edit uses macOS-only syntax and breaks on Linux
findings.body: sed -i '' -E ... is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed on Linux interprets the empty string as a filename and errors out, so updating an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in .env fails for Linux developers. Use a portable form (e.g. sed -i.bak and remove the backup, or detect the OS).

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared, unpinned tsx fetched via npx
findings.body: The script was changed from ts-node (declared in devDependencies) to 'npx tsx', but tsx is not declared in this package's dependencies. On a fresh/offline install npx will try to download an unpinned package from the registry, making the script non-reproducible and failing without network access; tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency or the ts-node invocation kept.

findings.title: New destructive deleteCache mutation has no tests
findings.body: This PR adds a mutation that deletes all CalendarCache rows for a credential, guarded only by the credential-ownership check in this new handler, plus the new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository method, with no tests covering: deleting one's own cache, rejecting another user's credentialId, and returning cache status per credential. A regression in the ownership where-clause would let one user purge another user's calendar cache without any test failing.
